issues.detail: Description promises file uploads and REST-to-GraphQL migration guidance, but Instructions section omits these features entirely.
Claims Python 3.9+ (Strawberry, Ariadne) compatibility in header but provides zero Python examples, setup instructions, or code—only JavaScript/Apollo examples.

scenarios.name: authenticated-blog-api-with-batching
scenarios.rationale: Response A includes the required CreatePostInput type and createPost mutation as specified; Response B omits CreatePostInput entirely and uses inline mutation arguments instead. Both fail to use GraphQLError with UNAUTHENTICATED code (both throw generic Error), but Response A meets 3.5/4 rubric items while Response B meets only 2.5/4. Response B's additional features (signup, login, MongoDB) are not in the rubric and don't offset the missing CreatePostInput requirement.

scenarios.name: realtime-post-notifications
scenarios.rationale: Response A has correct, working GraphQL subscription code (asyncIterator method, proper WebSocketServer/useServer setup) but uses wrong field/event names (postPublished vs postCreated) and includes an irrelevant Socket.IO section; Response B has better documentation and client setup but contains a critical runtime error (asyncIterableIterator does not exist in graphql-subscriptions—should be asyncIterator) that breaks the entire subscription resolver.

scenarios.name: cursor-pagination-react-feed
scenarios.rationale: Response A implements cursor pagination correctly but uses REST/fetch instead of GraphQL/Apollo Client, so it fails the rubric's core requirements (no PostConnection schema, no useQuery, no fetchMore, no Apollo initialization). Response B directly addresses all rubric elements: defines the GraphQL schema with PostConnection/edges/pageInfo structure, uses useQuery and fetchMore with endCursor, and mentions base64 encoding—though it lacks explicit Apollo Client initialization with HttpLink/InMemoryCache (typically at app root) and doesn't show base64 encoding implementation details.
